label: copy-phase input k (fed-back k token)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the input token is k, i.e. when the model's own previously-emitted k is fed back in. 100% of activations and mass fall inside this predicate. It never fires on k during the original phase or at <DEL>, and never on any other input token. It is silent on roughly half of copy-phase k inputs, and no simple variable separates those cases. Rate and magnitude go up with later recall position: about 20% of k inputs are active at recall_idx 1, versus 60-75% at recall_idx 3 and 7-8. Activation also rises with longer L. The top activations (about 0.9-1.0 of max) occur when k is the second-to-last original token being fed back late in a length-9 sequence, or at early-middle positions such as recall_idx 2-3. Restricting to recall_idx >= 2 raises precision only to 0.54. Which tokens are output next and whether k repeats change little.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: k, -, c, x, a, j; least: 0, p, l, <DEL>) and the next token to output (most: 0, f, z, g, j, c; least: u, n, -, k); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=7, t=17, recall_idx=8.
